note: Product-intent confirmation record (T58, session arena/7264f3c2-zone2, 2026-11-17). Built to the brief's requirement: 'For each submitted link, store the intended ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date, and source. Keep observed redirect targets in a separate field. Do not merge the two fields.' The intended half and the observed half are separate objects per link and are never combined: `intent` is what the brief is believed to want, `observation` is what a fetch on a dated read actually served. Where an official source does not bind a supplied code to a product, the intended field stays an explicit null with the reason - it is never inferred (ledger flag F-06; the ASIN definition is source A01). Published at intent.html.
associates_tag_note: The tag was supplied by the owner on 2026-11-17 and is embedded in the published product Special Links for P1/P2/P3 (see tools/link_builder.py ASSOCIATES_TAG). The supplied short links below are evidence records and deliberately carry no tag: they are observations, not shopping links.
validation_rule: Amazon Associates policy (Participation Requirements; source S02) ties attribution to the tag on the Special Link. Per the brief: test one link per product in the enrolled Associates workflow and confirm destination and tracking report before scaling. That test needs the owner's signed-in Associates session and is recorded per link below as null until the owner runs it; the paste-ready procedure lives on intent.html.
fields_rule: intent.intended_asin is a checkable 10-character identifier per Amazon's ASIN definition (source A01). Every supplied code below is 9 characters, so intended_asin is null everywhere with that recorded reason; merging the observed ASIN into this field would fabricate an intent the record does not hold.
